title: Processors implement IProcessor with onOperations receiving OperationWithContext items filtered by document type, scope, branch, and document ID
content:
A processor implements `IProcessor` with `onOperations(operations: OperationWithContext[])` and `onDisconnect()`. Each `OperationWithContext` pairs an `Operation` (action type, input, index, hash, timestamp) with `OperationContext` (documentId, documentType, scope, branch, ordinal for cross-document ordering, resultingState as JSON). `ProcessorFilter` has optional arrays: `documentType`, `scope`, `branch`, `documentId`. A field that is `undefined` or `[]` matches everything; a field with values matches when the operation's context value is in the array; all present fields must match. The `"*"` wildcard is honored **only in `documentId`** — in `documentType`, `scope`, and `branch` a literal `"*"` matches only an operation whose value is the string `"*"`, i.e. nothing real. To match all scopes, omit `scope` or set it to `[]`; never write `scope: ["*"]` (the codegen analytics template emits exactly that, and it silently matches no operations). The factory pattern: outer function receives `IProcessorHostModule` (shared resources), inner function receives `driveHeader` per drive, returns `ProcessorRecord[]`. By default processors replay all history; set `startFrom: "current"` to skip historical operations.

_Corrected 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: ProcessorFilter determines which ops a processor receives; factory creates instances per drive with configurable filters.
